name: EXIF / Metadata Stripper
description: Remove EXIF, GPS and other hidden metadata from JPGs before publishing or uploading — protects your privacy and shrinks the file.
body:
🕵️

Drop JPG images here or click to browse

GPS, camera, and editing history are removed

What gets removed

No images processed yet.
  • GPS location coordinates
  • Camera make, model and lens
  • Date and time stamps
  • Software and edit history
  • Thumbnail previews with embedded data
howto: Drop one or more JPG files onto the dropzone.
The tool re-encodes each image, writing only the pixel data and none of the EXIF/GPS/ICC metadata.
Review the log to see each file processed.
Click Download cleaned images to get everything in a ZIP.
Check the File Size Batch Checker to confirm the cleaned files are smaller.
features: Removes GPS, camera and software metadata
Batch processing of many JPGs at once
ZIP export of all cleaned images

faq.a: Cameras embed GPS coordinates, serial numbers and timestamps in your photos. Publishing those leaks your location and equipment. Stripping them protects privacy.
It re-encodes the image to remove metadata, so there is a minimal generation change. Use high quality output and the visible difference is negligible for web use.

faq.q: Does it work for PNG or WebP?
faq.a: PNG and WebP carry less metadata, but the tool focuses on JPG, where EXIF is most common. The Background Edge Checker and Format Converter cover other needs for those formats.

faq.q: Can I keep the metadata and still publish?
faq.a: You can, but it is not recommended — reviewers and the public can see where and when the photo was taken. Stripping is safer.
